ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has four waveform options of voltage changing with time. A is a rectangular square wave, with parts both above the horizontal time axis and below the horizontal time axis. B is a sine wave, also periodically crossing the horizontal time axis, with waveforms on both the upper and lower sides. C is a series of pulsating waveforms, the waveform bulging upward from the zero axis and then returning to the zero axis, never below the horizontal time axis. D is a triangular wave, the waveform also crossing the horizontal time axis, with both positive half-cycles and negative half-cycles. Reasoning: The characteristic of pulsating direct-current voltage is that the voltage magnitude changes periodically with time, but the polarity does not reverse, that is, the waveform should always be on the same side of the zero axis, usually nonnegative. A, B, and D all have parts below the time axis, indicating that the voltage reverses, so they are excluded. Although C pulsates and changes with time, it is never below the zero axis, matching the characteristics of a pulsating direct-current voltage signal. Therefore the answer is waveform C.
